Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

treatment noun

how someone is treated

also treat (someone), treat well, treat badly, special treatment, ill-treatment

classical

Cic. Att. 5.20.9: ā mē līberāliter tractātur
Cic. Q. fr. 2.4.5: eum nimis asperē tractat
Traupman 397

tractō, tractāre, tractāvī, tractātum

verb, first conjugation: with an adverb

treat (someone well, badly …)

Latin says how someone is treated with the verb and an adverb: līberāliter, honōrificē, asperē tractāre. Lewis & Short: “to treat, use, or conduct one’s self towards a person in any manner”.

Examples

  • … in officiō est et ā mē līberāliter tractātur

    (Nicanor) is doing his duty, and I am treating him generouslyCic. Att. 5.20.9

  • Marcellīnus autem hoc ūnō mihi quidem nōn satis facit, quod eum nimis asperē tractat

    Marcellinus disappoints me in this one thing, that he treats him too harshlyCic. Q. fr. 2.4.5

  • nec līberālius nec honōrificentius potuisse tractārī

    (he wrote that) he could not have been treated more generously or more honourablyCic. Fam. 13.27.2

Other words

  • tractātiō, tractātiōnis f. — handling, treatment

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.9 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 397

    Classically the handling of things (instruments, arms, a subject) rather than of people.

See also treatment, behave, kind.

SourcesLewis & Short: tracto · Lewis & Short: tractatio
